reviews.review:
I considered writing a very long review but I don't think anyone would read it in big 2025. Picked this game up wayy after beating Mass Effect just to get more Mass Effect before ME4.

Lore nerds, there is nothing for you here. Story appreciators, nothing. Companion lovers, again, you have no reason to play this game. Exploration? No, you'd think so, but no, nothing for you guys either. Base builders? Nope. In fact there is nothing engaging about Andromeda whatsoever, at any point, except the combat.

Andromeda makes Mass Effect combat more dynamic than ever, and is pretty fun. However, that only carries the game so far, and I think most people after 30-40 hours will either have finished the game as quickly as possible or will never finish it. That's OK, you already got everything out of the game you will get anyways.

100+ Hours, with probably a lot of AFK time, and I've finally completed everything, all Tasks, exploration, etc. in Andromeda.

It is very difficult to write this review as a Recommendation. I'll be blunt: Andromeda is only worth running through as quickly as possible, and even then, only if you really like the gameplay loop of Mass Effect.

Doing my job as a Mass Effect Andromeda Fan to say this is a great game, had the chance for great DLC if it had more support back in the day and in general the story is great Sci-Fi. It was made a while ago but compared to some titles that released more recently that have a similar premise, like Starfield, Andromeda still feels more polished in story, characters and visuals and I like to revisit it on other consoles when I get the chance. Currently postponing a PC upgrade so I just haven't had the chance on my current machine to replay as I shuffle parts around. Don't let out-of-box reviews put you off, there was patches almost immediately after and the story itself was always a fun one. The current state of the game means it's worth picking up on sale or if you have the money but unfortunately we don't get to see more of Andromeda at this time.

Do not go into this game with the expectations of a storyline as polished and heartaching as the trilogy. This game had a lot to live up to. And for what it is, there is a LOT in this game. I mean it took me 100 hours to complete. 

I completed everything but two task missions cause they glitched when I tried. It does have its weird glitches but a lot of games do. It brought a new alien into the ME universe that is utterly fascinating. It left itself open for another game. And overall once you stop comparing it to the trilogy, it has a lot of really cool game mechanics that I would love to see more of.

I think the game need a little more polish in the dialog and story and the romantic areas.

TL;DR:
Mass Effect: Andromeda is a shallow, bloated, and poorly written spin-off that fails to live up to the original trilogy. 
Despite 270+ hours of effort, I found little payoff. Weak characters, forgettable story, filler quests, and tokenism over substance. Not worth the Mass Effect name.

Detailed Review:

I spent over 270 hours trying to give Mass Effect: Andromeda a fair chance — it didn’t earn it.

The story is dull and highly linear. The illusion of choice is just that — most decisions barely influence anything. The main plot lacks impact, tension, or surprise.

Characters are flat. Companions are largely unlikable, with little emotional depth or growth. The romance options are unbalanced and delayed, with awkward pacing. Gil, for example, is written with no arc beyond his identity, which feels like lazy checkbox diversity rather than meaningful representation. Forced identity beats are common — a recurring theme with multiple NPCs across species.

Gameplay mechanics are average. Combat is passable, close to ME3, but lacks polish. 
Skills are underwhelming, often making little difference to playstyle or outcome.

Quest design is padded with meaningless errands — collect X minerals or Y plants across massive, empty zones. 
These add hours but little value. A few side quests and locations stood out, but they are exceptions.

In short, the game feels like a cheap AA spin-off. It tries to do too much without doing anything particularly well. Shallow writing, incoherent structure, and filler over substance. It had potential, but the execution failed.

A disappointment — not worthy of the Mass Effect legacy.
